Modification of Clouds (1803), that although clouds could be organised into distinct mod-

fixed conditions and could pass from one to another producing intermediate (e.g. cirrostra-

years since he published them, in both scientific media and general ones such as GM, which
adopted his terminology from 1809, and discussed his work in 1810 and 1811. S.’s own
observations on the climate in Italy in 1818, which include his observation of clouds and
their varied forms, do not adopt Howard’s nomenclature, though this is perhaps not sur-
